title: a native pin whose graph reaches a host module requirement fails to compile: a dependency on the JavaScript host is not a capability a Layer can supply
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin' names `TypeScript` explicitly; `Module<"node:fs">` is poc/src/targets/classify.ts's concrete spelling of the same JavaScript-host dependence, and `blocksNativePin` rejects `TypeScript`, `Module<...>` and `Host<...>` together. The SMITHERS1510 is declared rather than filtered because it is a cascade the language really does produce, per conformance/README.md. It is also unavoidable: a host dependence cannot be authored in .sm without tripping the rule that guards it — a host MODULE is untrusted-foreign (SMITHERS1510) and a host GLOBAL is refused outright (SMITHERS1601, area 20) — so the Module<...>/Host<...> branch of the pin rule can only be pinned in a two-diagnostic cascade. The `node:fs` binding is inspected and never called, which is what keeps the cascade to one companion diagnostic instead of the SMITHERS1101/1301/1505 foreign-call chain a call would add.
